Graffiti's potency lies in its subversive, guerrilla nature. Unlike wall art, which is typically organized and sanctioned, graffiti thrives on immediacy, spontaneity, and the risk of persecution Where wall art may take time and care, graffiti is often quick, requiring speed and anonymity due to the threat of detection Its purpose is to challenge power, counter surveillance, and inscribe messages that are otherwise censored or suppressed. The July   uprising brought neW dimensions 10 this medium of dissent.
